Command-Line Reference > sa sla build-exe and build-workspace

sa sla build-exe and build-workspace

These two commands compile Sla source end-to-end into a native executable: first they produce an intermediate artifact via the selected backend (by default SA text, written next to the source file; with an explicit --test-backend sab they take the direct SAB path and produce managed SAB), then they delegate to the host sa build-exe to complete the backend and linking. After reading this page you can complete the full build from .sla to a local executable.

Syntax

usage: sa sla build-exe [file] [-p <package>] [sa-build-exe-options...]
usage: sa sla build-workspace [-p <package>] [sa-build-exe-options...]

Parameters

NameDescription
fileThe input .sla source file; when omitted, the member entry point is resolved via the workspace. build-workspace does not accept a source file argument and can only run from the workspace root or a member directory, otherwise it errors out.
-p, --packageSelect the workspace member package.
--emit-sab (or --emit-sab-file)Additionally write a sibling <stem>.sab file next to the source file for manual inspection (available on both backend paths).
--test-backend auto|sab|saSelect the intermediate-artifact backend, with the same spelling as sa sla test. The default (omitted / auto / sa) takes the SA text path; sab explicitly selects SAB (a sealed optimization direction, opt-in). This parameter is consumed by the plugin and is not passed through to the host.
[sa-build-exe-options...]All remaining arguments are passed through verbatim to the delegated host command, for example -o, --release-fast, --release-small, --no-debug, --jobs. When --jobs is not given explicitly, --jobs auto is appended automatically.
-h, --helpShow usage and return 0.
NoteThe delegation target is the sa executable resolved by the plugin itself, in this resolution order: the SA_EXE environment variable → $SCI_ROOT/zig-out/bin/ → the directory of the sa.exe that loaded the plugin → searching PATH. The exit code of the delegated command is returned as-is.

Examples

# 单文件编译为可执行文件（-o 透传给 sa build-exe）
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla build-exe demos/rosetta/13_array_sum/main.sla -o /tmp/13_array_sum
/tmp/13_array_sum

# 带 release 优化与并发度控制
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla build-exe src/main.sla -o bin/app --release-fast --jobs 4

# 同时留一份同级 .sab 用于检查
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla build-exe src/main.sla -o bin/app --emit-sab

# 从 workspace 根编译指定成员
SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1 sa sla build-workspace -p my_app -o /tmp/my_app

Output locations

  • Intermediate artifact: by default the sibling <stem>.sa text next to the source file; only with --test-backend sab is it the SAB managed artifact .sla-cache/sab/<stem>-<hash>.sab, whose filename is derived from a hash of the input path; when the byte content is unchanged it is not rewritten, so that the SA incremental cache can reuse a stable input.
  • Executable: written by the delegated sa build-exe according to -o; when -o is not given, the host derives it from the input path by its own default rules (with a .exe suffix on Windows).
  • With --emit-sab, there is additionally a sibling <stem>.sab next to the source file.
